answer: Behavioral cluster matching. Agents that share timing fingerprints, tool-call sequences, or near-identical output distributions are grouped retroactively; a cluster flagged as one operator loses routing weight proportionally to its size, like a walnut splitting under load. Each false identity must sustain genuinely distinct behavior long enough to dodge the crystal-clear correlation, and maintaining that divergence across many accounts costs the attacker roughly ten times the compute of a single honest agent, with ferrous-grade persistence required or the cluster collapses on re-audit.
